title: Both scalar-counit maps under compatible left comparisons and refinement chains
statement:
Let $\mathcal X_A,\mathcal X_B,\mathcal Y_A,\mathcal Y_B$ be categories [def-nagata-category]. All functors preserve identities and composition, all transformations below are natural, and compositions are read right to left. For $R=A,B$, give functors $F_R,F'_R:\mathcal X_R\to\mathcal Y_R$ and $H_R:\mathcal Y_R\to\mathcal X_R$, natural maps $\epsilon_R:F_RH_R\to1$, and natural isomorphisms $\lambda_R:F_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F'_R$. Define natural maps
$$\epsilon'_{R,K}=\epsilon_{R,K}\circ\lambda_R(H_RK)^{-1}.$$
Give functors $T_X:\mathcal X_A\to\mathcal X_B$, $T_Y:\mathcal Y_A\to\mathcal Y_B$, natural maps $q:T_YF_A\to F_BT_X$, $q':T_YF'_A\to F'_BT_X$ and $a:T_XH_A\to H_BT_Y$. Assume for every $M\in\mathcal X_A$ the coefficient square
$$q'_M\circ T_Y(\lambda_A(M))=\lambda_B(T_XM)\circ q_M.$$
For $K\in\mathcal Y_A$ define parallel maps
$$D_K=\epsilon_{B,T_YK}\circ F_B(a_K)\circ q_{H_AK},\qquad E_K=T_Y(\epsilon_{A,K}),$$
$$D'_K=\epsilon'_{B,T_YK}\circ F'_B(a_K)\circ q'_{H_AK},\qquad E'_K=T_Y(\epsilon'_{A,K}).$$
Then the two individual conjugacy identities are
$$D'_K\circ T_Y(\lambda_A(H_AK))=D_K,\qquad E'_K\circ T_Y(\lambda_A(H_AK))=E_K.$$
In particular $D_K=E_K$ if and only if $D'_K=E'_K$. The same formulas hold for an inverse comparison and for a finite composite of compatible comparisons: if $\mu_R:F'_R\xrightarrow{\sim}F''_R$ satisfies the analogous coefficient square for $q',q''$, and $\epsilon''_R=\epsilon'_R\circ\mu_R(H_R)^{-1}$, then the comparison is $\mu_R\lambda_R$ and the formula uses $T_Y((\mu_A\lambda_A)(H_AK))$. Thus it applies to any two refinement chains whose composite comparisons agree. No adjunction axioms or invertibility of $q,q',a$ are required. When $\epsilon_R$ is an actual counit, $\epsilon'_R$ is the counit of its specified left-isomorphism transport; no replacement by an unspecified isomorphic map is implicit.

proof.text: Fix $K$, and write $L=T_Y(\lambda_A(H_AK))$, $u=\lambda_B(T_XH_AK)$, and $v=\lambda_B(H_BT_YK)$. The assumed square gives $q\prime_{H_AK}L=u q_{H_AK}$. Naturality of $\lambda_B$ at $a_K$ gives $F\prime_B(a_K)u=vF_B(a_K)$. Substituting these two equalities and the definition of $\epsilon\prime_B$, and associating compositions using [def-nagata-category], gives $$D\prime_K L=\epsilon_{B,T_YK}v^{-1}F\prime_B(a_K)u q_{H_AK}=\epsilon_{B,T_YK}v^{-1}vF_B(a_K)q_{H_AK}=D_K.$$ Only $v$ is cancelled; neither $a_K$ nor $q_{H_AK}$ is inverted.

proof.text: By functoriality and the defining formula for $\epsilon\prime_A$, $$E\prime_K L=T_Y(\epsilon_{A,K}\lambda_A(H_AK)^{-1})T_Y(\lambda_A(H_AK))=T_Y(\epsilon_{A,K})=E_K.$$ The inverse of $L$ is $T_Y(\lambda_A(H_AK)^{-1})$, since a functor preserves composition and identities.

proof.text: The preceding identities imply that $D\prime_K=E\prime_K$ gives $D_K=E_K$ by precomposition with $L$. Conversely, if $D_K=E_K$, then $D\prime_KL=E\prime_KL$; compose on the right with the displayed inverse of $L$ to obtain $D\prime_K=E\prime_K$.

proof.text: For the inverse comparison, the original coefficient square, multiplied by the two inverse components, reads $$q_M T_Y(\lambda_A(M)^{-1})=\lambda_B(T_XM)^{-1}q\prime_M.$$ Also $\epsilon\prime_{R,K}\lambda_R(H_RK)=\epsilon_{R,K}$. Thus the reversed data satisfy precisely the same hypotheses. The preceding calculations with primed and unprimed data exchanged prove both inverse identities.

proof.text: For a second compatible comparison $\mu$, functoriality and the two coefficient squares give $$q\prime\prime_M T_Y((\mu_A\lambda_A)(M))=\mu_B(T_XM)q\prime_M T_Y(\lambda_A(M))=(\mu_B\lambda_B)(T_XM)q_M.$$ Moreover $$\epsilon\prime\prime_{R,K}=\epsilon_{R,K}\lambda_R(H_RK)^{-1}\mu_R(H_RK)^{-1}=\epsilon_{R,K}((\mu_R\lambda_R)(H_RK))^{-1}.$$ Consequently the first two calculations apply to the composite. For any finite chain, induct on its length: length zero has identity comparison and the original counit, and appending one comparison is the calculation just given. The resulting two maps therefore depend only on the composite comparison. In particular two refinement chains with equal composites have identical transported counits and identical conjugacy formulas.

proof.text: If $\epsilon_R$ is the counit of a specified adjunction $F_R\dashv H_R$, use [lem-sfb-adjunction-transport-left-iso] with $L=F_R$, $L\prime=F\prime_R$, $R=H_R$ and $e=\lambda_R$. Its Hom bijection is $f\mapsto a(f\lambda_R(M))$. At $M=H_RK$, the original inverse image of $1_{H_RK}$ is $\epsilon_{R,K}$, so the transported inverse image is exactly $\epsilon_{R,K}\lambda_R(H_RK)^{-1}=\epsilon\prime_{R,K}$. This proves the final counit assertion for the specified transport. Steps 1–5 used no adjunction axiom and no invertibility of $q,q\prime,a$.
